subject: Chemistry
topic: Atomic size and ionisation enthalpy across the 3d series
title: Five More Protons, Same Size: Radius and Ionisation Enthalpy across the 3d Series
summary: Across the 3d series each new electron enters the inner (n−1)d subshell and shields the outer 4s electrons, nearly cancelling the extra nuclear charge. So atomic radii change only slightly and the first ionisation enthalpy rises slowly (631 → 906 kJ/mol), unlike across a normal period.

notes.title: 05 – Atomic Size and Ionisation Enthalpy across the 3d Series

keyPoints: Across a transition series the new electron enters the **inner (n−1)d** subshell and **shields** the outer ns electrons.
The extra nuclear pull and the extra shielding nearly balance: **radii change only slightly**, nearly constant in the middle.
**First ionisation enthalpy rises slowly**: 631 (Sc) → 906 (Zn) kJ/mol, versus about three times across period 3.
**Zn** has the highest IE (stable 3d¹⁰ 4s²); 4d and 5d radii are almost equal (lanthanoid contraction).

blocks.p: The nuclear charge rises by one at each step, but each added electron goes into the inner 3d subshell. It partly shields the outer 4s electrons from the added charge, so the effective pull on them grows only a little.
Across period 3 there is no such inner shielding: the first IE climbs from 496 (Na) to 1520 kJ/mol (Ar).
